The '''2010–11 Ligue 1 season''' was the 73rd since its establishment. Entering the season, [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] were the [[2009–10 Ligue 1|defending champions]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/l-om-champion-de-france.htm|title=L'OM champion de France!|date=5 May 2010|work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]]|access-date=5 May 2010|language=fr|archive-date=8 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008220057/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/l-om-champion-de-france.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> The fixtures were announced on 21 May 2010 and the season began on 7 August and ended on 29 May 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.francefootball.fr/FF/breves2010/20100521_103826_montpellier-bordeaux-en-ouverture.html |title=Montpellier-Bordeaux d'entrée |date=21 May 2010 |work=France Football |access-date=21 May 2010 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100524052144/http://www.francefootball.fr/FF/breves2010/20100521_103826_montpellier-bordeaux-en-ouverture.html |archive-date=24 May 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.francefootball.fr/FF/breves2010/20100517_181551_le-calendrier-2010-11-le-21-mai.html |title=Le calendrier 2010–11 le 21 mai |date=17 May 2010 |work=France Football |access-date=17 May 2010 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100520023648/http://www.francefootball.fr/FF/breves2010/20100517_181551_le-calendrier-2010-11-le-21-mai.html |archive-date=20 May 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The winter break was in effect between 23 December and 15 January 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url =https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1174615.html | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20121108230021/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1174615.html | url-status =dead | archive-date =8 November 2012 | title =French league confirm kick-off date|date=26 February 2010|work=FIFA |access-date=17 May 2010}}</ref> There were three promoted teams from [[2009–10 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]], replacing the three teams that were relegated from Ligue 1 following the [[2009–10 Ligue 1|2009–10 season]]. A total of 20 teams currently competes in the league with three clubs suffering relegation to the second division, [[Ligue 2]]. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for the season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.<ref name=bye>The DNCG is responsible for overseeing the legal and financial accounts of professional football clubs in France. If clubs operating in [[French football]] don't meet the DNCG's expectations, they can face sanctions, such as relegation.</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Actualités DNCG|url=http://new.lfp.fr/corporate/dncg|work=LFP|publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]]|date=26 May 2009|access-date=26 May 2009|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101019001943/http://new.lfp.fr/corporate/dncg|archive-date=19 October 2010|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In addition, German [[Sportswear (activewear)|sportswear]] company [[Puma AG|Puma]], whom the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] share a partnership with, provided a brand new match ball for the new season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Les ballons officiels Ligue 1 – Ligue 2 révélés |url=http://www.lfp.fr/actualiteLFP/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=13384 |work=LFP |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=5 June 2009 |access-date=5 June 2009 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090607073426/http://www.lfp.fr/actualiteLFP/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=13384 |archive-date=7 June 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Saison 2010/2011: les nouveaux ballons officiels Ligue 1 – Ligue 2|url=http://www.footpro.fr/corporate/article/saison-2010-2011-les-nouveaux-ballons-officiels-ligue-1-ligue-2.htm|work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]]|publisher=Foot Pro|date=12 May 2010|access-date=14 May 2010|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313202927/http://www.footpro.fr/corporate/article/saison-2010-2011-les-nouveaux-ballons-officiels-ligue-1-ligue-2.htm|archive-date=13 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Lille clinched the league title on 21 May 2011 with one match to spare after drawing 2–2 with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] away at the [[Parc des Princes]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Paris Saint-Germain v. Lille Match Report|url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53999|work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]]|date=21 May 2011|access-date=21 May 2011|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110524162322/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53999|archive-date=24 May 2011|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/295241?cc=5739|title=Lille seal historic title|date=21 May 2011|work=ESPN Soccernet|access-date=24 May 2011|archive-date=2 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120202024016/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/295241?cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3274/ligue-1/2011/05/21/2497525/lille-win-2010-11-ligue-1-title|title=Lille win 2010–11 Ligue 1 title|date=21 May 2011|work=goal.com|access-date=24 May 2011}}</ref>
The title was the club's third overall and its first in [[1953–54 French Division 1|over 57 years]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Le LOSC champion de France!|url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/le-losc-champion-de-france.htm|work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]]|date=21 May 2011|access-date=21 May 2011|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317100501/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/article/le-losc-champion-de-france.htm|archive-date=17 March 2012|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> As a result of Lille also winning the [[Coupe de France]] [[2011 Coupe de France Final|during the season]], the club became the third different club in three consecutive seasons to win some form of [[double (association football)|the double]] in France. In [[2008–09 Ligue 1|2009]], [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] captured the league and league cup double and, [[2009–10 Ligue 1|in the following season]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] did the same.

On 19 April, [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]] drew 0–0 with [[Nîmes Olympique|Nîmes]]. The draw assured Caen a return to Ligue 1 after falling down to Ligue 2 [[2008–09 Ligue 1|the previous season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Le SM Caen en Ligue 1! |url=http://www.starwizz.com/foot-caen-remonte-ligue-1-38678 |work=StarWizz |publisher=StarWizz |date=20 April 2010|access-date=5 May 2010}}</ref> On 30 April, [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]] secured promotion to Ligue 1, for the first time since being administratively relegated in [[1990–91 Division 1|1991]], following stalemates in matches involving [[FC Metz|Metz]] and [[Clermont Foot|Clermont]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Brest en Ligue 1! |url=http://www.le10sport.com/Football/Ligue2/Brest-en-Ligue-1-300435525.html |work=le 10 Sport|publisher=Le 10 Sport |date=30 April 2010|access-date=5 May 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100503155917/http://www.le10sport.com/Football/Ligue2/Brest-en-Ligue-1-300435525.html| archive-date= 3 May 2010| url-status= live}}</ref> Brest capped the promotion by defeating [[Tours FC|Tours]] 2–0 on the same day. On 14 May, on the final day of the Ligue 2 season, [[AC Arles-Avignon|Arles-Avignon]] became the last Ligue 2 club to achieve promotion to the first division. The club defeated fourth-place club Clermont 1–0 at home to earn promotion. The club had achieved promotion to Ligue 2 from the third-tier [[Championnat National]] the previous season meaning the club has jumped two divisions in just two seasons.

[[Grenoble Foot 38|Grenoble]] was the first club to suffer relegation to [[Ligue 2]]. The club's impending drop occurred on 10 April 2010 following the team's 4–0 defeat to [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]]. On 3 May 2010, both [[US Boulogne|Boulogne]] and [[Le Mans Union Club 72|Le Mans]] were relegated to Ligue 2 following defeats. Le Mans relegation was confirmed following their 3–2 loss away to [[AS Nancy|Nancy]], while Boulogne suffered relegation after losing 1–0 to [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]], who both Boulogne and Le Mans were trailing.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 Round up |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11816_6135490,00.html |work=Sky Sports |publisher=Sky Sports |date=5 May 2010 |access-date=5 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100508141935/http://www.skysports.com/story/0%2C19528%2C11816_6135490%2C00.html |archive-date=8 May 2010 |url-status=live }}</ref> Having earned promotion to Ligue 1 the previous season, Boulogne's return to Ligue 2 meant a short-lived stay in the highest division.

===Stadia and locations===
On 17 May 2010, the Ligue de Football Professionnel announced that, for the first time in [[French football]] history, two clubs, [[FC Lorient|Lorient]] and [[AS Nancy|Nancy]], would switch the surface of their football pitch from grass to [[artificial turf]]. This type of surface is common in North America and Eastern Europe, but is considered rare in Western Europe. Both clubs attributed the switch to weather and ecological problems with severe [[cold front]]s affecting their [[Regions of France|region]]s every winter. The switch would, in turn, reduce energy costs and also avoid cancellations of matches due to a frozen pitch. Also, in Lorient's case, a constant [[Cell growth|proliferation]] of [[earthworm]]s onto their pitch over the past two seasons had led to a rapid deterioration of the ground, which has forced the club to spend as much as €2 million to replace it. Both clubs previously toured Russia, [[Austria]], and [[Norway]] to become better acclimated with the surface.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lorient et Nancy, pionniers du synthétique |url=http://www.footpro.fr/corporate/article/lorient-et-nancy-pionniers-du-synthetique.htm |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |publisher=Foot Pro |date=17 May 2010 |access-date=20 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313202919/http://www.footpro.fr/corporate/article/lorient-et-nancy-pionniers-du-synthetique.htm |archive-date=13 March 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
